outcome: Write the GraphReFly kernel in Python against the D797 kernel rule set (activated by graphrefly:D798, revised by graphrefly:D799 and graphrefly:D801), move the existing Python facade from the Rust native engine onto it as graphrefly:D800 decides, and qualify each kernel scenario with source-bound Python evidence
acceptance: Scope: a new pure-Python kernel written directly against the rules active by graphrefly:D798/D799/D801 (graphrefly spec/rules.jsonl), not a migration of the PyO3 path. graphrefly reference/kernel and sessions/active/python-kernel-benchmark are read for behavior and structure only; the package kernel follows this repository's architecture, typing and Python idioms, and reference tests are not Python evidence.
Transition: until the package no longer imports graphrefly._native, CI, the release workflow and docs/release.md build against graphrefly-rs cf02fc9 instead of graphrefly-rs@main (graphrefly:D800).

Phase 1, messages: the private kernel package has the closed set START, PENDING, DATA, RESOLVED, INVALIDATE, COMPLETE, ERROR; there is no TEARDOWN, PAUSE, RESUME or PULL and no upward call on ctx. ctx.down rejects START, PENDING, RESOLVED (R-failure@3, graphrefly:D801), unknown types, a terminal that is not last, DATA SENTINEL and an ERROR payload that is SENTINEL or a bool, before anything is applied; uncaught, the rejection is the node's ERROR. Passes C-26, C-42, C-12 (c) and C-23 (f).

Phase 2, waves: the kernel puts PENDING first in every array carrying DATA, RESOLVED, INVALIDATE, COMPLETE or ERROR and marks the sender's dependents pending; a pending node that sent nothing gets exactly one kernel RESOLVED; a quiet node marks nothing pending. Each ctx.down call is one array in written order, split at its last INVALIDATE, delivered after the function returns; a fan-in runs once per wave. The snapshot is the values of the last array that carried DATA, then the terminal. A batch commit is one wave. Passes C-12, C-16, C-23, C-28, C-41 and the value and quiet-node clauses of C-44.

Phase 3, terminals and invalidation: COMPLETE, ERROR and INVALIDATE each have an auto or manual policy per node, default auto; under auto ERROR an INVALIDATE earlier in the wave applies first; under manual INVALIDATE ctx.deps[i] says whether an INVALIDATE arrived. A node that ends closes its lifetime at once and releases its dependencies; an ended node can still be subscribed and depended on, its snapshot carrying its terminal; host input to it is refused. Passes C-3, C-15, C-17, C-36, C-40 except its replace clause, the terminal and manual-INVALIDATE clauses of C-44, and C-34 except its cleanup clause.

Phase 4, lifetime: an optional setup, owned by the instance, runs once per lifetime just before the first run with that run's ctx and may return the lifetime's cleanup; there is no on_deactivation or on_invalidate. ctx gives the lifetime's abort signal. Closing aborts the signal, releases dependencies, runs the cleanup (which may still read private state) and drops private state, also when the node ends. Output and requests through a closed lifetime's ctx are dropped; status is derived. Passes C-4, C-33 and C-34.

Phase 5, requests: host inputs, subscribe, unsubscribe, replace, rewire and batch commits made during a wave wait and run in order after it. batch(body) runs body at once and returns its result; its commit is one wave and itself a request, its topology requests run after the commit, a throwing body commits nothing, and an async body is refused. set with a function computes from the value when the write runs, and a function returning its argument (identity) writes nothing. replace(id, deps, fn, setup, recipe) gives a new instance under the same id and subscribers; definition(id) reads it. ctx.rewire(deps) changes only the node's own dependencies for its lifetime and is undone when it closes; there is no graph-level rewire. Cycle checks look through current and declared dependencies. Passes C-6, C-11, C-29, C-35, C-37 and the replace clause of C-40.

Checkpoint phase, only after the user admits the checkpoint module: checkpoint is implemented in Python over the kernel's seed, definition and recipe as the admitted module rule states, and the public checkpoint and restore API is carried onto it, so the cut-over does not withdraw it. Passes the checkpoint clauses of C-38 that the admitted module covers.

Cut-over, after phase 5 and the checkpoint phase: the public facade (Graph.state/derived/node/effect/subscribe/batch, Node.cache, the D428 exception taxonomy, the D477/D480 async runners and re-entry queue, the network sources, retain, and checkpoint and restore once that phase is done) runs on the Python kernel; every public API change is recorded first as a graphrefly-py decision shown to the user. The wire facades (wire_bridge, wire_edge_group, wire_bridge_protobuf, wire_bridge_ack_driver and their status, issue and timeout types) are withdrawn at the cut-over by a graphrefly-py decision shown to the user first, and Python stops claiming C-1a and C-1c until phase 6. Then the package no longer imports graphrefly._native, pyproject.toml drops maturin for a pure-Python build backend, the release builds a pure-Python wheel, and AGENTS.md, docs/development.md, docs/index.md, docs/README.md and docs/release.md stop saying that Rust owns the native engine.

Phase 6, cross-graph, after the cut-over and once the root has settled the bridge model: the wire bridge, WireEdgeGroup, the ack-timeout driver and the canonical protobuf codec are implemented in Python over the kernel; the codec passes every D497 golden vector in graphrefly spec/fixtures/protobuf; the bridge releases every edge of one cause together as one batch in the peer graph, and wire-edge frames say PENDING. Passes C-1 and C-1b, and C-1a and C-1c are re-qualified on the Python implementation. The wire facades return on this implementation.

Failure semantics: an Exception from a node function or setup is that node's ERROR, surfaced publicly as GraphCallbackError; a sink callback Exception is a SubscriberCallbackError and never a node ERROR; a fatal BaseException (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit and others) propagates to the caller and becomes neither, since the kernel catches only Exception. Async work enters only at source, runner and adapter boundaries, never inside a synchronous wave.
Sugar: the first-run gate (and any dynamic reads or equality dedup the package adds) may stay, and the docs say it is Python sugar, not protocol.

Each phase ends with the package suite (uv run pytest), uv run ruff check ., uv run mypy src and that phase's scenarios passing, plus a reference measurement of the graphrefly sessions/active/python-kernel-benchmark bench.py scenarios on this kernel (time per node run; not a gate); it is then committed and pushed to the branch d797-kernel-migration (graphrefly-py:D3). Nothing is pushed to main, no pull request is opened and nothing is merged.

Evidence: each scenario is reported with runtime py, the test command, the result and the source commit, recorded on this item. Root spec/conformance.jsonl runtimes flags are not changed here (graphrefly:D784); the root records the evidence. Scenarios that also check a draft module rule (C-2, C-5, C-9, C-10, C-13, C-24, C-27, C-30, C-31, C-32, C-38, C-39, C-43) are out of scope.
